children: , the consumer-technology and services giant, faced a labor disruption in Italy on the same day it rolled out the iPhone 18 Pro worldwide. Shares were down a bit to $333.95, keeping the market reaction muted despite the high-profile timing of the strike.

Three unions said more than 1,600 workers across 17 Apple stores were covered by the action, or roughly 94 employees per location on average. Their demands include more hiring, permanent contracts for temporary workers and the option for part-time employees to increase their hours. Apple said its Italian stores stayed open, limiting the immediate operational hit during one of the company's most important product-launch days.

The bigger question is whether labor pressure becomes a recurring cost around Apple's premium retail model. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at 1,489 in Italy, so smooth store execution matters when Apple is asking customers to pay top-tier prices. The valuation picture also leaves little room for disappointment: the chart shows Apple at $333.95 versus a GF Value estimate of $286.32, putting the stock 16.64% above that benchmark. At that premium, investors are effectively paying for strong execution to remain the norm.

title: Apple Stock Drops as 1,600+ Italian Workers Strike on iPhone 18 Pro Launch
